exposure: history of abortions, still birth, and early neonatal deaths
registration of pregnancy after 8 weeks of gestation
history of maternal fever prior to the week of delivery
mode of delivery by cesarean section, forceps or vacuum
time of birth during on-call hours
cohort: Neonates diagnosed with sepsis (n = 240) and neonates not diagnosed with sepsis (n = 240) born during the same period in secondary and tertiary care hospitals of a district in Sri Lanka.
finding: Several modifiable risk factors, including history of pregnancy loss, late pregnancy registration, limited antenatal visits, maternal fever, prolonged leaking amniotic fluid, multiple vaginal examinations, meconium stained amniotic fluid, operative delivery, birth during on-call hours, male sex, and low birth weight, were independently associated with neonatal sepsis.
mod_finding: Cesarean section, forceps, or vacuum delivery was associated with increased odds of neonatal sepsis.
